models_evaluated: AI 3 (masked; vendors Leben Care Health Services, Retinal AI Diagnostic Software, SigTuple Technologies)

links.outcome: Head-to-head comparison of vendor DR algorithms on same local images before selection
links.effect: Sensitivity 60%-80% and specificity 14%-96% across algorithms; FDA-approved algorithm excluded for low specificity; AI-3 selected (specificity 96.01%, sensitivity 68.42%, accuracy 88.43%).
links.quote: One Indian AI algorithm declined participation, and an Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved algorithm was excluded due to low specificity in interim analysis.

links.outcome: Local diagnostic performance of commercial DR algorithms versus human reference standard
links.effect: Wide variability; AI-3 sensitivity 68.3% below FDA 85% benchmark; one algorithm detected DR in 89.2% of eyes vs 27.48% by reference standard.
links.quote: The three AI algorithms demonstrated variable diagnostic performance, with sensitivity (60%-80%) and specificity (14%-96%).

links.outcome: Change in AI-3 performance from validation to real-world implementation site
links.effect: Sensitivity rose from 68.4% to 99.6% while specificity fell from 96% to 64.7%; DME sensitivity only 26.5%.
links.quote: The AI-3 algorithm’s sensitivity increased significantly from 68.4% to 99.6%, while specificity decreased from 96% to 64.7% between the validation and implementation phases.

links.outcome: AI flagging of ungradable/cataract-affected images
links.effect: Gradability specificity 8%; 21 (42%) cataract eyes deemed ungradable by humans were categorized gradable by AI.
links.quote: Notably, the AI-3 algorithm failed to detect 21 (42%) eyes with cataracts, categorized as gradable.

links.outcome: Two-week pre-implementation integration testing of hardware, connectivity, workflow
links.effect: Testing identified technical issues and bottlenecks, leading to improved connectivity, mandatory clinical variables, faster turnaround, and local data storage.
links.quote: The two-week testing at PGIMER and DH Mohali validated the full AI workflow, identified technical issues, assessed reliability in clinical settings, and highlighted data and reporting bottlenecks.

unlisted_practices: Darkroom setup to achieve physiological mydriasis and reduce ungradable nonmydriatic images
Monthly kappa monitoring of operator image acquisition learning curve
Telephonic follow-up of AI-referred patients to assess referral adherence

links.outcome: Commercial algorithms' diagnostic performance against human grading
links.effect: Across three algorithms, sensitivity ranged from 60%-80% and specificity from 14%-96%, demonstrating substantial differences between candidate products.
links.quote: The three AI algorithms demonstrated variable diagnostic performance, with sensitivity (60%-80%) and specificity (14%-96%).

links.outcome: Preimplementation identification of technical and data-flow problems
links.effect: Two-week testing identified technical issues and data/reporting bottlenecks, prompting refinements to connectivity, mandatory clinical variables, result turnaround, and local data storage.
links.quote: The two-week testing at PGIMER and DH Mohali validated the full AI workflow, identified technical issues, assessed reliability in clinical settings, and highlighted data and reporting bottlenecks.

links.outcome: Missed diabetic macular edema and referable diabetic retinopathy
links.effect: DME sensitivity was 26.5%; referable DR sensitivity was 78.9% and specificity was 98.1%.
links.quote: However, sensitivity is relatively low (26.5%); for detecting RDR, sensitivity and specificity were 78.9% and 98.1%.

links.outcome: Diagnostic performance changes between validation and implementation
links.effect: Between validation and implementation, sensitivity increased from 68.4% to 99.6%, while specificity decreased from 96% to 64.7%.
links.quote: The AI-3 algorithm’s sensitivity increased significantly from 68.4% to 99.6%, while specificity decreased from 96% to 64.7% between the validation and implementation phases.

links.outcome: Failure to identify ungradable fundus images
links.effect: Image-gradability sensitivity was 100%, but specificity was 8%, indicating poor recognition of ungradable images.
links.quote: For image gradability, the AI’s sensitivity was excellent at 100%, but specificity was low (8%) ( Table 2 ).

unlisted_practices: Train and supervise optometrists in fundus-image acquisition, with longitudinal monitoring of image quality.
Improve fundus-image gradability through controlled lighting, darkroom acclimatization, ergonomic adjustments, and equipment reinforcements.

links.outcome: Diagnostic performance across competing vendors
links.effect: Testing candidate models on the same data identified the best-performing tool (accuracy 88.43%) for implementation.
links.quote: AI 3 showed the best performance with specificity of detecting DR, 96.01% (93·24‐97·72); sensitivity, 68.42% (59·71‐76.05); PPV, 86.67% (78.31‐92.26); accuracy, 88.43%; and agreement with the RS (κ=0·65) and was selected for implementation (Table S2 in Multimedia Appendix 1 ).

links.outcome: Identification of technical and workflow issues
links.effect: A two-week acceptance testing phase effectively identified technical issues, connectivity problems, and data and reporting bottlenecks before live rollout.
links.quote: The two-week testing at PGIMER and DH Mohali validated the full AI workflow, identified technical issues, assessed reliability in clinical settings, and highlighted data and reporting bottlenecks.

links.outcome: Model specificity on local population
links.effect: Local validation prevented the deployment of an FDA-approved algorithm that exhibited unacceptably low specificity on the local patient population.
links.quote: One Indian AI algorithm declined participation, and an Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved algorithm was excluded due to low specificity in interim analysis.

unlisted_practices: Fine-tuning candidate models on evaluation feedback prior to full clinical implementation
Training allied health professionals (optometrists) to capture and interpret AI-supported screening images
